1. `/` now 302 redirects to `services.app.box.com` (was 206 before)
2. `/graphql` returns 503 with Box-format JSON error (different backend from Express)
3. All other paths hit Express with CSRF tokens, `access-control-expose-headers: Server-Timing`, and clickjacking protection
4. OPTIONS on `/graphql` returns 503 (no CORS preflight handling)

## Analysis for notes.services.box.com

**Surface map discovered this cycle:**

| Path | Backend | Status | Notes |
|------|---------|--------|-------|
| `/` | Envoy → redirect | 302 → services.app.box.com → app.box.com | Root no longer serves Notes; consolidated into main app |
| `/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling` | Socket.IO (Engine.IO v4) | **200** — live | Accepts unauthenticated handshakes, returns session IDs, upgrades to websocket |
| `/api/2.0/*`, `/graphql/*`, `/*` | Express | 404 | CSRF cookies set on every request; `access-control-expose-headers: Server-Timing` present but NO `access-control-allow-origin` |
| `/graphql` | Box API backend | 503 | Returns Box-format JSON error |
| `/realtime` | nginx → upstream | 502 | Dead backend behind nginx |
| OPTIONS on root | Envoy | 204 with wildcard `*` (no credentials) | Standard secure |
| OPTIONS on `/socket.io/` | Socket.IO | 400 `{"code":0,"message":"Transport unknown"}` | No CORS preflight handling |
| OPTIONS on Express paths | Express | 404 with same headers as GET | No CORS preflight handling |

**Key observations:**

1. **Socket.IO accepts unauthenticated sessions** — Engine.IO v4 handshake returns `sid`, `upgrades: ["websocket"]`, `pingInterval: 7000`, `pingTimeout: 15000`, `maxPayload: 5000000` with no auth token required. This is standard Socket.IO design (auth happens post-handshake via events), but the server has **no CORS restrictions** — it accepts any Origin. While same-origin policy prevents reading responses cross-origin, the ability to establish sessions without auth could be leveraged if an attacker can control a subdomain.

2. **Incomplete CORS configuration on Express backend** — `access-control-expose-headers: Server-Timing` is set globally (even on 404s) but `access-control-allow-origin` is absent. This is a dead CORS middleware layer — not exploitable as-is, but signals potential misconfiguration if routes are added.

3. **CSRF tokens set on every request** — `_csrf` (HttpOnly) and `csrf-token` (readable by JS) cookies are set on ALL requests including 404s. Standard double-submit cookie pattern.

4. **Wildcard CORS at root** — OPTIONS on `/` returns `access-control-allow-origin: *` (no credentials). Not exploitable without credentials.
